questions.prompt: A tool result in the record turns out to be wrong. What does an append-only log do about it?
options: It edits the old fact so the record shows the right value
It removes the old fact and appends the right one
It appends a new fact with the right value and keeps the old one
It clears the record and starts the turn again
questions.explanation: Old facts never change. The correction goes at the end, so the record shows both the wrong answer and the fix in the order they happened.

questions.prompt: Why does all() return a copy of the list instead of the list itself?
options: So a caller cannot remove or reorder facts in the real record
Because a copy is faster to read than the original
Because Object.freeze only works on copies
So the model receives a smaller request
questions.explanation: Freezing protects each fact, but the list itself could still be changed. Returning a copy means only append() can change the real list.

questions.prompt: In the bank statement picture, what stands for the agent's current chat history?
options: The balance, which comes from adding up the lines
questions.explanation: The balance is not stored on its own; it comes from reading every line. In the same way, the agent works out its history by reading every fact in its record.
